newsitem.title: CHINA: CCT Telecom aims to develop China paging.
newsitem.headline: CCT Telecom aims to develop China paging.

text.p: CCT Telecom Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it was aiming to make huge strides into China's paging market following a deal with a Ministry of Electronics Industry-linked company to form joint ventures in China.

CCT China Ltd, which will be 67 percent owned by CCT Telecom and 33 percent owned by Tesonic International Ltd, is set to create three Sino-foreign joint ventures which will acquire assets owned by Tesonic Communication Co Ltd, Tesonic Satellite Network Co Ltd and Tesonic Electronics Co Ltd.
The assets are currently owned by Tesonic Industrial, a mainland collective ownership enterprise, which will have a 10 percent stake in the ventures.
Tesonic Satellite has been granted a nationwide VSAT (Very Small Aperture Terminal) business operating license by China's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications.
"It is one of the six enterprises being granted the operating licence in China," Lu Chang Hong, chairman of Tesonic Industrial, told a news conference.
He said Tesonic Industrial provided services to more than 130 VSAT terminal stations in China. "Its popularity will be like using mobile phones in the future."

Lu said CCT China would seek cooperation and strategic alliances with the VSAT operators to develop the business in the Asia Pacific areas, positioning itself ahead of deregulation in the telecommunications market.
VSAT applications would focus on three main areas: paging services, multimedia networks and real time data transmission, Tesonic Industrial's technical consultant Stephen Lai said.
He saw strong growth potential in the paging area.

"As VSAT will cover all areas in the (Asia-Pacific) region, paging services operators which use this technology will not need to invest a huge sum of money in setting up stations and installing cables," Lai said.
"More and more mainland paging operators are using this technology," he added.

CCT China also aims to set up of a nationwide sales network for products such as fax machines, cordless phones in China and conduct research and development on fixed UHF digital radio link communication equipment to serve rural telecommunications needs in China. It also intends to provide commercial customers with turnkey telecommunications systems, Lu said.
Lu said CCT China would also lease telecommunications equipment and provide management services to Tesonic Satellite for the operation of its VSAT network services businesses.

Tesonic International is 60 percent owned by Time Line and 40 percent owned by China National Electronics Import and Export Corp, a state-owned enterprise wholly owned by the Ministry of Electronics Industry.

News that CCT Telecom would set up joint ventures with the company to produce and distribute telecommunications equipment and networks and provide management consultancy services to China's satellite industry sent shares of CCT Telecom up HK$0.43 to HK$1.78 on Thursday.
"It will help the company expand into the China market, boost its reputation and broaden its earnings base," said Clement Mak, chairman of CCT Telecom
He said strategic investor Xinhua News Agency, which bought a 12.51 percent stake in the company last month, had helped to arrange the deal.
